headline: Marchenko traded to Maple Leafs from Blue Jackets, signs six-year deal
title: Maple Leafs acquire Kirill Marchenko in trade with Blue Jackets for Matthew Knies

body:
<forge-entity title="Kirill Marchenko" slug="kirill-marchenko-8480893" code="player">Kirill Marchenko</forge-entity> has a new home.

The 26-year-old forward was traded to the Toronto Maple Leafs from the Columbus Blue Jackets on Monday as part of a six-player deal that saw <forge-entity title="Matthew Knies" slug="matthew-knies-8482720" code="player">Matthew Knies</forge-entity> go back to Columbus.

Marchenko, who could have become a restricted free agent after this season, signed a six-year, $75 million contract ($12.5 million average annual value) with the Maple Leafs that starts next season, according to his agent.

“I think the most simple way I can put it is there’s a lot of good players in the NHL, (but) very few that can impact winning and can singlehandedly dictate the outcome of games,” Toronto general manager John Chayka said Tuesday, when the Maple Leafs play their season opener against the Montreal Canadiens at Scotiabank Arena (7 p.m. ET; TVAS, SN). “We believe Kirill is one of these players for us. You’ve got to give up quality to get quality, and we gave up some quality people and quality players.

“He was a player that wasn’t willing to just go anywhere. He wants to win. He wants to be part of a world-class organization.”

Chayka said he's hopeful Marchenko can make his Maple Leafs debut Tuesday, provided his immigration paperwork is completed.

In addition to Marchenko, the Maple Leafs also acquired forward <forge-entity title="Miles Wood" slug="miles-wood-8477425" code="player">Miles Wood</forge-entity> and goalie <forge-entity title="Elvis Merzlikins" slug="elvis-merzlikins-8478007" code="player">Elvis Merzlikins</forge-entity>. Going to Columbus with Knies was forward <forge-entity title="Steven Lorentz" slug="steven-lorentz-8478904" code="player">Steven Lorentz</forge-entity> and defenseman <forge-entity title="Emil Andrae" slug="emil-andrae-8482126" code="player">Emil Andrae</forge-entity> and a second-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft.

Marchenko is entering his fifth season since being selected by the Blue Jackets in the second round (No. 49) of the 2018 NHL Draft. He had 67 points (27 goals, 40 assists) in 76 games in 2025-26, leading Columbus in goals and finishing second in points. He has led the Blue Jackets in goals each of the past three seasons. 

Marchenko has 208 points (102 goals, 106 assists) in 292 NHL games. He has one year remaining on a three-year. $11.55 million contract ($3.85 million average annual value) he signed with Columbus on July 28, 2024.

“His ability to make plays and score goals … great shot, right-handed shot, (he) gives us different options for the power play and throughout the offensive zone,” Chayka said. “To get a top scorer in his prime, be able to lock him up through those prime years at a number that is effective for us, we thought it was a special opportunity.”

Knies, 23, had an NHL career-high 66 points (23 goals, 43 assists) in 79 games for the Maple Leafs last season. He signed a six-year, $46.5 million contract ($7.75 million AAV) with Toronto on July 1, 2025.

“I was a little bit shocked, just of the timing of it all,” Knies said Tuesday. “But I think with my name being out there and just kind of the uncertainty here, I feel like it was just kind of an inevitable the way it seems. So yeah, it was pretty shocking in the sense that we just came home from practice (Monday), and obviously I had an opening game tomorrow, so really didn't see it happening.”

Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell said, “We wouldn't make this trade if we didn't think we were helping our hockey team, and we truly believe that for multiple reasons this deal is going to make us a better team today and moving forward.”

Waddell said the deal got done just before the 5 p.m. ET deadline on Monday to submit Opening Night rosters. 

“If you'd asked me that question on Saturday (about the trade gettiing done), I could have said no, and then Sunday it started looking like there was something that might make sense here, and again, I wasn't on that timetable," Waddell said. "It wasn't I had to do this yesterday or next week. I said all along if we're going to do it, we’ve got the deal that we can accept and feel good about  and that came about in you know the 24 hours Sunday to Monday.”

“Toronto called me Sunday morning and wanted to revisit it and that led into Monday. … The roster had to be in by five,  and the trade finished at 4:59 with 50 seconds or something, with 10 seconds to get our roster in there when the trade finished. Actually, I just saw that on video earlier today. I knew it was close, but it was a process.”

Selected by the Maple Leafs in the second round (No. 57) of the 2021 NHL Draft, Knies has 160 points (67 goals, 93 assists) in 240 regular-season games and 14 points (eight goals, six assists) in 27 Stanley Cup Playoff games. 

“I apologized to him for all the noise over the last several months,” Chayka said of Knies. “I don’t think it was necessarily fair to him. This was the only thing (potential trade involving him) we seriously considered as a management crew. 

“These things happen. He understands that as a professional athlete. He’s a smart kid. But he took the news well. It’s a good young team he’s going to. I think it’s a good fit for him.”

Merzlikins, 32, was 14-11-3 with a 3.40 goals-against average and .883 save percentage for Columbus. He’s 108-111-38 with a 3.22 GAA and .900 save percentage in 274 regular-season games, all with Columbus.

Wood had 14 points (eight goals, six assists) in 54 games last season and has 196 points (99 goals, 97 assists) in 567 regular-season games with the New Jersey Devils, Colorado Avalanche and Blue Jackets.

Lorentz had 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 71 games with Toronto last season. A member of the 2024 Stanley Cup champion Florida Panthers, the 30-year-old has 80 points (36 goals, 44 assists) in 381 regular-season games with the Carolina Hurricanes, San Jose Sharks, Panthers and Maple Leafs.

Andrae, 24, had 13 points (two goals, 11 assists) last season for the Philadelphia Flyers. He was traded to the Maple Leafs on June 16 as part of the Joseph Woll trade.

The Blue Jackets open their season at home against the Buffalo Sabres on Thursday (7 p.m. ET; CBJHN, CBJNHL, MSG-B).

“I think it was it was always Hell going and to play against these guys, with how strong and fast they are,” Knies said. “I think a lot of this team is built on physical components and just how they can outmuscle and outstrength, outskate every team that comes in there to play.”

*NHL.com staff writer Mike Zeisberger and independent correspondent Craig Merz contributed to this report*
